Title: Microservices instead of modular monolith
Decision: Use independently deployable Django (native HTTP, no DRF) microservices for identity, content, engagement, points, moderation and supporting functions.
Alternatives: Modular Django monolith; service-oriented shared deployment
Rationale: Independent scaling, ownership and blast-radius containment; fits explicit product direction.
Consequences_and_risks: Distributed tracing, network latency, service auth, operational complexity and consistency overhead.
Mitigations_and_followups: Maintain service contracts, per-service CI/CD, distributed tracing and runbooks.
Acceptance_evidence: Service inventory and deployment independence demonstrated

Title: Docker Swarm orchestration
Decision: Deploy containerized services and workers using Docker Swarm stacks, overlay networks, secrets and rolling updates.
Alternatives: Kubernetes; standalone Docker Compose; Nomad
Rationale: Chosen deployment platform and comparatively simple operating model.
Consequences_and_risks: Manager quorum, limited native policy features, overlay troubleshooting and ecosystem constraints.
Mitigations_and_followups: Restrict manager control plane; pinned images; secrets; backup manager state; test upgrades.
Acceptance_evidence: Swarm recovery and rollout drills

Title: Host Nginx on Swarm manager — AWS staging reconciliation
Decision: Host-installed Nginx stays outside Swarm on the manager; AWS is the current staging target under the full-application mandate. Historical Oracle topology is superseded for staging. Production transport/HA decisions remain open.
Alternatives: Dedicated third VM; Nginx in Swarm
Rationale: Reuses two existing Oracle VMs under the pilot budget, keeping Nginx outside the Swarm service lifecycle.
Consequences_and_risks: Co-location increases shared blast radius and means VM1 or manager failure also interrupts ingress; not high availability.
Mitigations_and_followups: Harden VM1, restrict origin ports, verify Tunnel endpoint and upstream TLS, reserve host resources, implement backup/restore and outage recovery.
Traceability: DOC-201, DOC-202, DOC-203, DOC-208; docs/architecture/ADR-003_007_Implementation_Reconciliation_2026-11-01.md; full application mandate section 3; PHASE-02_Data_Ownership_Review.md
Acceptance_evidence: VM1 Nginx systemd and config check; Swarm node audit; origin-bypass and upstream transport tests

Title: Flutter mobile clients
Decision: Build Android and iOS applications using Flutter/Dart.
Alternatives: Separate native apps; React Native
Rationale: One shared mobile codebase and consistent UX.
Consequences_and_risks: Platform-specific secure storage, lifecycle and plugin vulnerabilities require testing.
Mitigations_and_followups: MASVS checks, secure token storage, release signing and dependency review.
Acceptance_evidence: Mobile security test matrix

Title: Django templates web frontend
Decision: Use Django templates with HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript for the administrator/moderator console only. Flutter serves all non-privileged users; public web is limited to approved static legal/deletion/app-link resources (mandate section 3).
Alternatives: Next.js SPA; React SPA
Rationale: Matches approved stack and reduces client complexity.
Consequences_and_risks: CSRF, session security and BFF design need care.
Mitigations_and_followups: Strict CSRF/CSP, session cookie settings, no secret in browser, web service deployment separation.
Acceptance_evidence: CSRF and browser security tests

Title: PostgreSQL with service data ownership
Decision: Use PostgreSQL; each microservice owns its logical data store and credentials, with no direct cross-service writes.
Alternatives: Shared schema; separate physical database server per service; NoSQL
Rationale: Transactional guarantees and strong isolation semantics while allowing initial shared hardware.
Consequences_and_risks: Distributed consistency, outbox delivery and cross-service reporting complexity.
Mitigations_and_followups: Per-service roles/databases, migration ownership, outbox/inbox, reconciliation.
Acceptance_evidence: Cross-service privilege negative tests

Title: RabbitMQ broker with Celery workers
Decision: Use RabbitMQ as private Celery message broker for background tasks; persist authoritative business events in PostgreSQL transactionally and use outbox/inbox plus idempotent consumers. Redis is not a required component of this design.
Alternatives: Redis; Kafka; database polling alone
Rationale: Matches the user-confirmed deployment choice and the Django/Celery stack.
Consequences_and_risks: RabbitMQ is not an authoritative database; delivery can be duplicated or interrupted, and a single broker is not HA.
Mitigations_and_followups: Private listeners, per-service credentials and vhosts, TLS where appropriate, durable queues/messages, manual acknowledgements where compatible, bounded retry, dead-letter queues, resource alarms, monitoring, backups and replay tests.
Acceptance_evidence: Verify broker placement and health, credential isolation, worker flow, retry/dead-letter/replay and outage recovery

Title: Managed video processing and streaming
Status: Superseded for R1 VOD — OD-07 approved 10 Nov 2026 (private R2 + FFmpeg Content worker; live streaming out of R1)
Decision: Use managed Cloudflare video processing/streaming rather than running self-managed transcoders; exact product/plan subject to commercial validation.
Alternatives: Self-hosted FFmpeg pipeline; alternative managed provider
Rationale: Reduces operational risk and media-processing attack surface.
Consequences_and_risks: Vendor dependence, pricing, egress, playback access control and webhook behavior.
Mitigations_and_followups: Provider proof-of-concept, signed callbacks, direct upload intents and data-processing review.
Acceptance_evidence: Provider integration and cost acceptance

Title: Server-authoritative engagement and non-cash points
Decision: Award non-cash points only after backend-qualified genuine engagement; append-only auditable postings; never award for ad clicks/views.
Alternatives: Client-calculated points; ad-event rewards; mutable balances
Rationale: Fraud resistance and ad-policy separation; respects approved R1 scope.
Consequences_and_risks: Higher implementation cost; fraud false positives and disputes.
Mitigations_and_followups: Versioned rules, evidence references, dedupe, reversals, review workflow.
Acceptance_evidence: Replay, concurrency, fraud and ad-event zero-award tests

Title: Release sequencing and financial separation
Decision: R1 creator-content with non-cash points; defer business verification R2, ticketing R3 and financial settlement/payouts R4.
Alternatives: Build all verticals in R1
Rationale: Limits launch risk and separates financial regulatory scope.
Consequences_and_risks: Future schema and integration changes require forward compatibility.
Mitigations_and_followups: Feature gates, isolated future contexts and separate monetary ledger design.
Acceptance_evidence: R1 endpoints cannot issue cash payouts

Title: Public gateway and internal service access
Decision: Expose only a dedicated public API gateway/BFF through Nginx; internal service APIs are private and workload-authenticated.
Alternatives: Expose every service behind Nginx; API gateway vendor
Rationale: Reduces public attack surface and centralizes routing.
Consequences_and_risks: Gateway may become a bottleneck and failure point; gateway auth cannot replace object authorization.
Mitigations_and_followups: Horizontal scaling, per-service auth, audience scopes, rate limits and health checks.
Acceptance_evidence: Gateway failover and unauthorized route probes

Title: Service-to-service identity
Decision: Use mutually authenticated transport and short-lived scoped service credentials, with explicit audience restrictions.
Alternatives: Shared static API keys; trust overlay network
Rationale: Reduces lateral movement and credential replay.
Consequences_and_risks: Certificate issuance/rotation complexity and clock synchronization.
Mitigations_and_followups: Select certificate/identity issuer; automate rotation and revocation.
Acceptance_evidence: Expired, wrong-audience and forged identity tests

Title: Client authentication and sessions
Status: Design approved — implementation and verification open
Decision: The owner approved the Django-native authority and v1.0 mobile/web session and privileged MFA design. Executable contract and verification remain open.
Alternatives: Django-native selected; managed OIDC or bespoke auth not selected
Rationale: Django-native identity uses the existing Django/DRF identity service. The approved design specifies separate mobile and browser session controls and privileged MFA.
Consequences_and_risks: Incomplete session and MFA controls and missing verification evidence block production acceptance.
Mitigations_and_followups: Implement and verify approved lifetimes, refresh rotation, logout and revocation, mobile storage, web sessions and CSRF, MFA, recovery, key rotation and abuse protections.
Acceptance_evidence: Owner design approval recorded 2026-11-01; DOC-206 execution evidence remains open

Title: Nginx-to-Swarm private transport
Decision: Choose a private routed connection or WireGuard tunnel with verified upstream TLS/mTLS and restricted ports.
Alternatives: Public Swarm ingress with TLS; VPN only; private LAN
Rationale: Avoids direct public exposure of application nodes.
Consequences_and_risks: Depends on VM/network placement and certificate lifecycle.
Mitigations_and_followups: Choose topology, document CIDRs and firewall ACLs, test interception.
Acceptance_evidence: Network diagram, firewall audit and MITM test

Title: Swarm control-plane sizing and availability
Decision: Select manager count and worker capacity based on budget and availability target; 3 managers for quorum HA where feasible.
Alternatives: Single manager; 3 managers; 5 managers
Rationale: Availability requirements must be balanced against budget.
Consequences_and_risks: Single manager is SPOF; 2 managers do not provide robust fault tolerance.
Mitigations_and_followups: Capacity plan, node placement, manager backups, failure simulations.
Acceptance_evidence: Quorum and node-loss drill

Decision: Choose managed vs self-hosted PostgreSQL, primary/replica model, PITR, encrypted backups and approved RPO/RTO.

Rationale: Data durability and recovery goals must be quantified before pilot.

Title: Observability and audit pipeline
Status: Mechanism approved — Decision D (25 Nov 2026, docs/planning/Owner_Decisions_A-J_2026-11-25.md) approves centralized structured logs without secrets, monitoring and alerts; retention values, alert thresholds and implementation evidence remain open (#145) (was: Proposed — needs approval)
Decision: Centralize structured logs, metrics, traces and append-only security audit records with trace IDs.
Alternatives: Per-container logs only; vendor APM; open-source stack
Rationale: Necessary to investigate cross-service incidents and fraud.
Consequences_and_risks: Sensitive data exposure and storage cost.
Mitigations_and_followups: Redaction, retention, role restrictions, alert thresholds and audit integrity.
Acceptance_evidence: End-to-end trace and redaction tests

Title: Secrets, images and CI/CD controls
Decision: Use Swarm secrets or external secret store, pinned images, vulnerability scans, SBOMs and gated production deployments.
Alternatives: Environment variables; mutable latest tags; manual SSH deploy
Rationale: Protects production and improves release provenance.
Consequences_and_risks: Maintenance and operational overhead; Swarm secrets lifecycle needs design.
Mitigations_and_followups: Rotation runbooks, image provenance, rollback, two-person production approval.
Acceptance_evidence: Secret scan and unsigned-image rejection

Title: Qualified view and points parameters
Status: Partially approved — DEC-003 restricted-pilot parameters approved 10 Nov 2026; general-release parameters open
Decision: Define genuine-view thresholds, dedupe windows, exclusions, points conversion and dispute windows before implementing award logic.
Alternatives: Fixed per-view points; weighted quality; periodic scoring
Rationale: Rules must be explicit, fair, auditable and resistant to gaming.
Consequences_and_risks: Prematurely freezing a formula creates fraud or product-policy risk.
Mitigations_and_followups: Approve rule table, thresholds, versioning, privacy impact and test fixtures.
Acceptance_evidence: Approved rule examples and boundary tests

Title: Privacy retention and data residency
Status: Mechanism approved — Decision C (25 Nov 2026, docs/planning/Owner_Decisions_A-J_2026-11-25.md) approves the privacy request, deletion, legal-hold and configurable retention-schedule mechanism; retention periods and data residency remain open and need legal approval (#136) (was: Open — legal/product decision required)
Decision: Approve purpose-based retention, deletion/appeal workflows and provider data-processing terms before pilot.
Alternatives: Indefinite retention; minimum necessary retention
Rationale: Privacy-by-design and incident response evidence balance.
Consequences_and_risks: Legal review and provider commitments outstanding.
Mitigations_and_followups: Retention matrix, legal review, data subject procedures and deletion tests.
Acceptance_evidence: Privacy review and deletion/hold tests

Title: Nginx high availability and TLS ownership
Decision: Choose Cloudflare-to-Nginx TLS and origin authentication, upstream encryption, and whether a second Nginx VM is needed for pilot.
Alternatives: Single proxy; dual proxy behind LB
Rationale: Ensures trustworthy proxy headers and continuity.
Consequences_and_risks: HA increases cost; single proxy outage impacts all clients.
Mitigations_and_followups: Document certificate ownership, renewals, failover, edge allowlist.
Acceptance_evidence: Origin-bypass, expiry and failover tests

Title: API versioning and event contracts
Decision: Use /api/v1 versioning, OpenAPI 3.1 for HTTP, schema-versioned internal events, consumer compatibility checks.
Alternatives: Unversioned endpoints; protobuf-only; ad hoc events
Rationale: Supports independently deployed microservices.
Consequences_and_risks: Version drift and duplicated schema management.
Mitigations_and_followups: Canonical DOC-205 and packages/contracts/events/catalogue.yaml; Phase 2 review candidate, approval pending #305/#141; implemented parity plus planned non-exposure checks.
Acceptance_evidence: Backward-compatibility CI test
